explanations: Yes. markProcessed is annotated REQUIRES_NEW, so the dedup row commits in its own transaction before inventory.reserve runs. If reserve throws (for example InsufficientStockException or a DB error), the listener does not ack and the error handler redelivers the record, but the event is already recorded, so markProcessed returns false and the retry is acknowledged as a duplicate. The reservation is silently lost. The dedup insert must be in the same transaction as the business effect (or the record removed on failure).

Duplicates that matter here are the same event published more than once; they land at different offsets, so an offset key would not detect them, while eventId is stable. The consumer name is part of the key, covering the cross-group case. Index speed and compaction behaviour are not the reason.

The unique key makes the insert the arbiter: one instance gets inserted == 1 and proceeds; the other gets 0 and skips. Consumer groups give no such guarantee across a rebalance or redelivery. The stock UPDATE would simply succeed twice if stock allowed, and the error handler is per-container.

After the crash the processed_events row exists, so markProcessed returns false and the listener acks and returns; the reservation committed earlier stays as the only one. Nothing in the config routes to a dead-letter topic, and the duplicate path returns before reserve is called, so no reservation insert conflict arises.
